language_check.method: Script screen only; Latin-script languages are not automatically distinguished from English.

windows.quote:
For eight weeks, I read a chapter before looking at my phone in the morning. I expected the change to help me remember more of what I read. At the end of the eight weeks, I could recall the plots of three novels, but I had not tested my memory before the experiment. I therefore cannot tell whether my recall actually improved.

The change I noticed was simpler: I stopped interrupting a chapter to check messages. I liked that. I still checked my phone as soon as I finished, and on two mornings I skipped reading altogether. This was a routine I tried, not a rule I consistently followed.

I am reluctant to recommend the same routine to everyone. My mornings were quiet during those weeks, and I did not try it when I was travelling. The reading itself was worthwhile to me even without evidence of a memory benefit. Next month I want to try reading after dinner instead, although I have not chosen a start date.

known_limitations: In the saved 36-document English pilot, high-score false positives occurred on human writing. Do not treat a near-1 score as established authorship.
notes: Four-class model outputs are not proof of authorship or percentages of words.
AI involvement = ai + ai_edited + humanized; human is the mutually exclusive class.
Multi-window document aggregation has not been calibrated; document probability is unavailable.
The model card's threshold at 0.5% FPR is a vendor benchmark setting, not a local guarantee.
Short passages, translations and unfamiliar domains can be unreliable.

occlusion.interpretation: Sensitivity to deleting a paragraph. Positive delta means removal lowered the score; length/context changes confound this. This is not causal authorship evidence or a sentence probability.
